identity.title: Computationally Efficient RL under Linear Bellman Completeness for Deterministic Dynamics

problem.claim: Design computationally and statistically efficient reinforcement-learning algorithms for the linear Bellman complete setting.

gap.claim: Although prior work established statistical tractability, whether a computationally efficient algorithm exists remained open.

contributions.claim: Provides a computationally efficient algorithm for linear Bellman completeness covering large action spaces, random initial states, and random rewards when the underlying dynamics are deterministic.
Uses noise injected into least-squares regression to perform optimistic value iteration, with noise restricted to the training-data null space.
Designs the noise to preserve optimism while circumventing a subtle error-amplification issue.

stated_novelty.claim: The work addresses the previously open computational-efficiency question by providing an algorithm under the stated deterministic-dynamics conditions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an algorithm that handles large action spaces, random initial states, and random rewards, subject to deterministic underlying dynamics.
The authors report that null-space noise is designed to ensure optimism while avoiding a subtle error-amplification issue.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies efficient reinforcement learning with linear function approximation in the linear Bellman complete setting, which includes linear MDPs and LQRs.
It identifies a gap between known statistical tractability and unknown computational efficiency.
It presents a computationally efficient algorithm under deterministic dynamics, despite broad action, initialization, and reward conditions.
The approach injects carefully designed null-space noise into least-squares regression for optimistic value iteration.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific algorithmic mechanism—null-space noise—to two targeted goals: preserving optimism and avoiding error amplification.

lessons.interpretation: A compact mechanism-to-obstacle explanation can make a technical contribution legible without detailing the full algorithm.
lessons.application: When presenting a new method, state which component addresses which named technical difficulty, and preserve the conditions under which the claim applies.
lessons.exception: This framing is insufficient when the abstract must establish quantitative guarantees or empirical performance, which are not reported here.

unknowns: The abstract gives no computational or statistical complexity bounds, theorem conditions beyond deterministic dynamics, or empirical results.
It does not specify how the method scales with action-space size or quantify the claimed error-amplification avoidance.
